title: Why is space silent?
sources: NASA Sound in Space Educational Review

lines.text: In Hollywood sci-fi movies, exploding starships make deafening roaring booms, but in real space, there is zero sound.
lines.caps: Why is outer space in *complete | absolute *silence?

lines.text: Sound cannot travel without a physical medium to carry its vibrations.
On Earth, sound travels when vibrating vocal cords or speaker cones bump neighboring air molecules together.
lines.caps: On Earth sound waves *push | neighboring air *molecules

lines.text: Deep space is a near-perfect vacuum containing only a handful of hydrogen atoms per cubic meter.
lines.caps: Space is a *near-vacuum | with virtually zero *matter

lines.text: With no atmospheric molecules to bump into each other, sound waves simply cannot propagate.
lines.caps: With no molecules to *vibrate | sound cannot *propagate!

lines.text: Even if a gigantic supernova exploded right next to your spaceship window, you would hear absolute dead silence.
lines.caps: Even a giant *supernova | explodes in total *silence

lines.text: In outer space, the famous tagline is true: no one can hear you scream.
lines.caps: In space, no one can *ever | hear you *scream!
